Naomi / Marcus —

Below is a compact, numeric-first response you can send to Alicia. I also attached a spreadsheet (redwood_capacity_hedge.xlsx) with the full calculations and alternate sensitivity runs. High level: we offer a standard commit + true-up approach, plus two distinct hedge options.

1) Baseline billing model (example)
- Baseline committed volume: 200,000,000 tokens/month
- Committed unit price: $0.70 / 1K tokens (applies to tokens up to commit)
- Overage band 1 (200M - 500M): $1.10 / 1K tokens
- Overage band 2 (500M - 1.5B): $1.65 / 1K tokens
- Overage band 3 (>1.5B): $2.30 / 1K tokens

Worked month (numbers):
- Baseline usage: 200M tokens (covered at commit)
- Spike day 1: +1.2B tokens (distributed across band 2)
- Spike day 2: +1.2B tokens
- Remaining month dynamic workload: 150M tokens
- Total month usage = 2.75B tokens

Invoice calculation (monthly):
- Committed covered: 200M @ $0.70/1K = $140.00k
- Overage allocation: 2.55B tokens -> split into bands: 300M @ $1.10k = $330k; 1.5B @ $1.65k = $2,475k; 750M @ $2.30k = $1,725k (note: bands iteratively applied)
- Gross monthly charge = $4,670k
- Monthly True-up: if prior months had credit buffer it nets here; standard monthly net invoicing applies and annual reconciliation can be requested for committed variance adjustments.

2) Capacity hedge options
A) Prepaid Burst Cushion (monthly amortized credit)
- Structure: Customer prepays for an allocated burst cushion (e.g., 2B tokens/month cushion) billed upfront and amortized over 12 months as a negative credit against overage charges.
- Pricing: Premium of 25% over standard overage blended rate for the purchased cushion capacity.
- Reconciliation: Unused cushion tokens at year-end can be rolled forward (one-time) or refunded at 40% of purchase price.
- Example impact: Purchasing 2B cushion at blended overage baseline ($1.50/1K) -> effective amortized monthly credit ~= $250k; reduces month invoice by cushion coverage until exhausted.

B) Reserved Capacity Hedge (annual)
- Structure: Annual reserve commitment (e.g., 4B tokens/year) at a discounted committed rate ($0.55/1K) which can be used to offset monthly spikes.
- Benefit: Lower committed $/1K and predictable capacity. Remaining reserve at year-end can be credited back at 60% of rate or rolled into next year at client option.
- Reconciliation: Annual True-up with option to convert unused reserve to discounted credits.

3) Mid-term tier movement and discounts
- If Velocity increases committed tier mid-term, the new tier price applies pro-rata from the effective change date.
- Discounts ladder: we apply step-discounts when monthly committed run-rate crosses threshold for a sustained period (>= 3 months). One-time promotional overrides can be applied for initial 6 months for new deals.
- Early termination or downward mid-term adjustments: standard breakage terms apply; unused prepaid cushion is subject to the refund schedule above.

4) Operational notes and SLAs
- Burst cushions do not guarantee placement on dedicated pools; if dedicated capacity is required that is a separate Dedicated SKU with guaranteed throughput and SLA.
- We support monthly billing with itemized token breakdown and per-route cost tables. All usage is auditable via the Console and included in monthly export.

I attached the spreadsheet with the worked numeric permutations and a one-page summary you can send to Velocity. Let me know if you want a third option that mixes monthly amortization and quarterly true-ups.

-- Karthik

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the questions. Please find a concise summary below and attached materials (Proposal v1 + worked calculations). If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk the numbers.

Executive summary (two options):
1) Standard commit + monthly True-up (simple, lowest operational friction)
   - Commit: 200M tokens/mo @ $0.70 / 1K tokens
   - Overage bands: $1.10 / $1.65 / $2.30 per 1K as usage grows (banded, iterative)
   - Monthly invoicing with itemized token buckets; annual reconciliation available on request

2) Capacity Hedge (recommended for unpredictable spikes)
   - Option A: Prepaid Burst Cushion — purchase an amortized cushion (e.g., 2B tokens) that offsets overages, 25% premium, unused funds partially refundable at year end.
   - Option B: Reserved Capacity Hedge — annual reserve at committed pricing ($0.55 / 1K) with annual True-up and crediting on unused reserve.

Worked example: see attached spreadsheet (redwood_capacity_hedge.xlsx). Bottom line: with a 2B prepaid cushion amortized over 12 months the effective invoice for the month in Alicia's example reduces by roughly 5–8% depending on band crossing. The Reserved Capacity option yields a larger unit discount but requires an annual commitment.

Next steps:
- We can produce a redlined commercial appendix for Velocity's legal team with either Option A or B.
- Please confirm which hedge option you prefer (None / Prepaid Cushion / Reserved Hedge) and whether you want us to include an annual reconciliation clause.

Thanks — happy to talk through this live.

Best,
